title: Kőnig's theorem: bipartite matching number = vertex-cover number (formalize-only)
why_not_classical: Kőnig 1931: in a finite bipartite graph the size of a maximum matching equals the size of a minimum vertex cover. Settled min-max theorem. Value is a Mathlib contribution (Matching.lean has IsMatching; no vertex-cover predicate and no ν=τ). Hall's marriage theorem is already upstream as set-family SDR — different statement. Do NOT re-fund as novel. Dilworth is a poset corollary and is NOT this bet.

statement_pin_required.convention: Fix G : SimpleGraph V, Fintype V, G.Colorable 2. IsVertexCover C := every edge is incident to C. Claim: max matching edge-card = min vertex-cover card. Easy inequality ν ≤ τ holds for all graphs; equality needs bipartite.
landmines: Do NOT cite HallMarriageTheorem as König — SDR ≠ ν=τ, even if one reduces to the other.
Not Kőnig's edge-colouring theorem (χ'=Δ bipartite). Not König's lemma (infinite trees). Not Tutte.
Matching number counts matching EDGES, not |M.verts| (twice as large).
Do not expand v1 into Dilworth.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: D. Kőnig, Gráfok és mátrixok, Mat. Fiz. Lapok 38 (1931) 116–119. Textbook: Diestel / Bondy–Murty König min-max. Type pin: Mathlib Subgraph.IsMatching + Colorable 2.
